definitions.explanation: A filler word used when thinking, hesitating, or trying to recall something. Buys time while formulating a response.

examples.japanese: えーと、⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何|なん}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦でした→です：09485_desu⟧⟦っけ→っけ：10739_kke⟧。
examples.english: Um, what was your name again?

examples.japanese: えーと、⟦{確|たし}か→確か：00894_tashika⟧⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}います→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: Let me see, I think it was tomorrow.

examples.japanese: えーと、⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
「⟦{電話番号|でんわばんごう}→電話番号：10159_denwabangou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧？」「えーと、090⟦の→の：09472_no⟧...」

えーと、⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{話|はな}していた→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦ん→の：09472_no⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦っけ→っけ：10739_kke⟧。⟦そう→そう：01167_sou⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧、⟦{来週|らいしゅう}→来週：00746_raishuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Um, what were we talking about? Oh right, the trip next week.

notes:
USAGE: One of the most common Japanese filler words, equivalent to English "um," "uh," or "let me see." Used across all registers but more common in casual speech.

FORMS:
- えーと: standard form
- ⟦ええと→ええと：23425_eeto⟧: written variant
- ⟦えっと→えっと：20056_etto⟧: shorter, more casual
- えーっと: lengthened for longer pauses

PRONUNCIATION: The ー indicates vowel lengthening. Can be drawn out further when needing more thinking time.

SIMILAR FILLERS:
- ⟦あのー→あのー：06911_anoo⟧: more polite filler, and the standard way to open a request to a stranger
- ⟦そのー→そのー：noentry⟧: similar hesitation filler
- ⟦なんていうか→なんていうか：15140_nanteiuka⟧: "how do I say this"
- ⟦ほら→ほら：06912_hora⟧: when prompting the listener to recall something

CULTURAL NOTE: While filler words exist in all languages, excessive use in formal Japanese (speeches, presentations) is considered less professional. Native speakers often use fillers less in polished speech.
